body:
GitHub issue #204.

## Problem

`ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS=1` is documented and reasoned about as a per-edit, deliberate
override, but through a harness env block it is SESSION-LIFETIME: loaded into the
agent process, it stays set after the settings file is deleted, silently bypassing
every railed path for the rest of the session with no in-session signal. Adjacently,
the rails test harness spawns the hook with `{ ...process.env, ...env }`, so an
ambient `ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS=1` inverts ~43 of 57 deny-tests to passing-as-allow — a
gate whose own suite is disarmed by the same variable that disarms the gate.

## Required behavior (per the issue's highest value-to-risk directions (1) + (3),
plus observability and honest docs)

1. HERMETIC TESTS (AC1): the rails test harness scrubs `ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS` from the
   child env unless a test sets it explicitly, so the suite passes identically
   whether or not the variable is set in the ambient environment.
2. SCOPED BYPASS (AC2): accept `ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS=<glob>` that authorizes ONLY rail
   hits whose path matches the glob; a hit outside the scope is still DENIED, so a
   bypass cannot silently authorize edits outside the scope it was granted for. The
   bare `ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS=1` form is kept for backward compatibility as a
   session-wide, unscoped override.
3. OBSERVABLE (AC3): a bypassed (allowed) edit emits a visible in-session notice
   (systemMessage) naming the scope and the session lifetime — not only the
   after-the-fact manifest line — so a stale bypass is seen, not inferred. The bare
   `=1` notice states plainly that it is UNSCOPED and session-wide and that deleting
   a settings file does not revoke it.
4. HONEST DOCS (AC4): docs/integrations/claude-code.md states the actual lifetime
   and scope of the bypass (session-lifetime for a harness-env override; scoped
   form available; unset + restart to revoke).

## Acceptance criteria

1. The rails suite is hermetic w.r.t. ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS: a deny-test still denies
   even when the variable is set in the PARENT process env. Verify: a test sets
   process.env.ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS='1', runs a rail edit, and asserts DENY.
2. `ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS=<glob>` allows a rail edit whose path matches the glob
   (recorded to the manifest) and DENIES a rail edit outside the glob, naming the
   scope in the denial. Verify with an in-scope and an out-of-scope case.
3. A bypassed edit emits a systemMessage naming the scope; the bare `=1` notice
   states it is unscoped/session-wide and unrevocable by deleting settings. Verify
   by asserting the emitted output.
4. `ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS=1` still authorizes any rail hit (backward compatible), and
   the unaudited-bypass refusal (record failed → deny) is preserved for both forms.
5. docs/integrations/claude-code.md documents the actual lifetime and the scoped
   form. Verify by reading the doc.
6. Full claude-code hooks segment green and `npm run preflight` green.

## Constraints

- Do NOT change the deny DECISION for the non-bypass path, the trust-root freeze,
  or the fail-closed-on-unverifiable-rails contract.
- The audit requirement is unchanged: an override (scoped or `=1`) is honored ONLY
  if durably recorded to the gate-manifest; an unrecordable override is refused.
- Scope-matching uses the same glob semantics (globMatch) the rails use.
title: ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS: hermetic tests, scoped bypass, in-session observability, honest lifetime
